config: Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B SDPA, 800 pairs, LR 1e-5, complex floor 0.60

across_seed.note: The mean across seeds is a mean of proportions, not itself a binomial sample; no Wilson interval is attached to it. Per-seed Wilson intervals are given above.

seed_variance_floor.interpretation: An effect smaller than the across-seed range of the quantity it is measured on cannot be distinguished from seed choice on a single seed.

comparison_design_note: Two different noise floors apply and must not be confused. A PAIRED within-seed comparison (baseline vs trained inside one run) cancels seed choice, so the relevant floor is same-seed run-to-run variability, observed at about two functions. An UNPAIRED comparison between two separately trained runs does not cancel it, so the relevant floor is the across-seed range measured here. Comparing a paired gain against the unpaired range would be the wrong test and would understate a real effect.

effects_reassessed.verdict: SURVIVES - the gain is positive in every seed and exceeds the same-seed floor in every seed. Pairing controls for the baseline's across-seed swing, and notably the TRAINED result is far more stable across seeds than the untrained one.

effects_reassessed.effect: complexity floor K1 vs K0 (+4, seed 42 only)
effects_reassessed.design: unpaired between two separately trained runs
effects_reassessed.verdict: DOES NOT SURVIVE - an unpaired 4-function difference measured on one seed, against an across-seed range of 7. The WEAK ACCEPT cannot stand without running K0 and K1 on seeds 43 and 44.

effects_reassessed.effect: checkpoint sweep peak step 60 vs step 50 (+4, seed 42 only)
effects_reassessed.design: within one run, but comparing two checkpoints
effects_reassessed.verdict: MARGINAL - 4 functions against a same-seed floor of about 2. Worse, the best step is not stable across seeds, so selecting a checkpoint by peak kill rate on one seed is not reliable.
